elements.text: FBG-SEANet: frequency-band graph construction and diagnosis
OCF / notch filtering suppresses operational components (illustrative).
Obtain signals in each frequency band. Graph construction then builds one subgraph per band and connects the subgraphs into the total graph.
EA feeds GCN₁; first pooling branches to two IR readout paths.

M and N vary (number of sensors / bands).
All graph connections are schematic; not a numerical adjacency matrix.
5-class output is illustrative (not fixed).
Author-lab figure: IR; published abstract: SR — terminology unresolved.
Lee et al., Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence 179 (2026), 115273  |  DOI: 10.1016/j.engappai.2026.115273

figure_contract.evidence_scope: C01 Image-first V4.1 presentation Stage-A candidate. Sensor count M and frequency-band count N vary independently. The author-visible Nth subgraph is normalized as B_N; this is an explanatory label, not a claim that the source figure prints the literal string B_N. Band-pass filtering yields per-band signals; graph construction forms one subgraph per band and connects the subgraphs into the total graph. The total-graph ellipsis and non-attached dashed continuation rail indicate omitted intermediate bands without asserting a B3-to-B_N node edge. One dashed inter-band connector is a schematic example only. Class outputs are square illustrative markers, not a fixed class count. Author-lab figure labels readouts IR; published abstract uses SR; equivalence unresolved. The five output squares are source-visible and intentionally unlabeled; no individual C₁–C₅ labels are asserted.
